verses.text: Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came to Jesus from Jerusalem. They asked,
"Why do your followers break the old rules handed down by our leaders? They do not wash their hands before they eat!"
Jesus replied, "And why do you break God's command for the sake of your own rules?
God said, 'Honour your father and mother,' and 'Anyone who speaks evil of their father or mother must be put to death.'
But you say that people can tell their father or mother, 'The help you might have received from me is a gift set aside for God.'
Then they do not need to honour their father or mother. In this way you cancel God's word for the sake of your own rules.
You hypocrites! Isaiah was right when he spoke God's message about you:
'These people honour me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me.
Their worship of me is worthless. They teach rules that were made up by human beings.'"
Jesus called the crowd to him and said, "Listen and understand.
What goes into a person's mouth does not make them unclean. It is what comes out of their mouth that makes them unclean."
Then the followers came to him and asked, "Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?"
He replied, "Every plant that my Father in heaven did not plant will be pulled up by the roots.
Leave them alone. They are blind guides. If a blind person leads a blind person, both of them will fall into a pit."
Peter said, "Explain this saying to us."
"Do you still not understand?" Jesus asked them.
"Do you not see that whatever goes into the mouth goes into the stomach and then out of the body?
But the things that come out of a person's mouth come from the heart, and these make a person unclean.
Out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual sin, stealing, lying and insults.
These are what make a person unclean. But eating without washing your hands does not make you unclean."
Jesus left that place and went to the area of Tyre and Sidon.
A Canaanite woman from that area came to him, crying out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter has a demon and is suffering terribly."
But Jesus did not say a word to her. So his followers came to him and begged him, "Send her away. She keeps shouting after us."
He answered, "I was sent only to the people of Israel, who are like lost sheep."
But the woman came and knelt in front of him. "Lord, help me!" she said.
He replied, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
"Yes, Lord," she said, "but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master's table."
Then Jesus said to her, "Woman, you have great faith! What you have asked for will be done." And her daughter was healed at that moment.
Jesus left there and went along the Sea of Galilee. Then he went up on a mountainside and sat down.
Large crowds came to him. They brought people who could not walk, people who were blind or disabled, people who could not talk, and many others. They laid them at his feet, and he healed them.

The people were amazed when they saw that those who could not talk were speaking, the disabled were made well, those who could not walk were walking and the blind could see. And they praised the God of Israel.

Jesus called his followers to him and said, "I feel sorry for these people. They have been with me for three days now and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint on the way."
His followers said, "Where could we get enough bread in this lonely place to feed such a big crowd?"
"How many loaves do you have?" Jesus asked. "Seven," they replied, "and a few small fish."
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
Then he took the seven loaves and the fish, and he gave thanks. He broke them and gave them to the followers, and they gave them to the people.
They all ate and had enough. Afterwards the followers picked up seven baskets full of the pieces that were left over.
Four thousand men ate, as well as women and children.
After Jesus had sent the crowd away, he got into the boat and went to the area of Magdala.
